questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A bulb is glowing with power equal to 110 W and potential difference 220V. Find the number 
of electron flowing per unit second

options.A:
y axis represents magnetic field. x axis represents distance from centre of axis of wire $[\mathrm{x}<\mathrm{a}]$ (a = radius of wire) & (I) \\
\hline
options.B:
y axis represents magnetic field. x axis represents distance from centre of axis of wire [ $\mathrm{x}>\mathrm{a}$ ] ( $\mathrm{a}=$ radius of wire) & (II) \\
\hline
options.C:
y axis represents magnetic field. x axis represents distance from centre of solenoid & (III) \\
\hline
options.D:
y axis represents magnetic susceptibility. x axis represents intensity of magnetisation & (IV) \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

Ans. $\quad \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{IV}, \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{II}, \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{III}, \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}$
Sol. $\quad \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{IV}, \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{II}, \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{III}, \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}$
Theoretical
16. A bulb is glowing with power equal to 110 W and potential difference 220V. Find the number of electron flowing per unit second

Ans. $\quad 3.2 \times 10^{18}$
Sol. $\quad \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{VI}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
I=\frac{P}{V} \\
I=\frac{110}{220}=\frac{1}{2} \\
\frac{n e}{t}=I \\
\frac{n}{t}=\frac{I}{e} \\
\frac{n}{t} \quad \frac{10}{2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \\
\frac{n}{t}=3.2 \times 10^{18}
\end{array}$$
